items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: I find it hard to believe that it was Max Steiner. Why Max Steiner would have wanted to involve himself with the second half of a jazz band chart I could never begin to understand why.

ctx.x: Tell me about the planned recording session and the one that finally came into being.

The planned recording session was the one of all the new music. It would have been "Dalvatore," "There's No You", "Out of This World," "Gray Suede," "Hey Look I'm Dancing," "Key F" and two more; "Memphis In June" and "Over The Rainbow." When I got back the only ones they had done were "Dalvatore" and half of "Over The Rainbow"; the other half was completed by--I find it hard to believe that it was Max Steiner. Nobody else--I guess Jack McKenney--said that he thought it was Johnny
